notes.title: Timber, plaster and a red floor
notes.summary: Notes on the palette for an office in Coimbatore: dark timber, warm plaster walls and a deep red floor.
notes.body:
An office is used for long hours, so the palette had to be calm before it was striking. Dark timber gives the room its weight, warm plaster softens the light from the windows, and the red floor ties the open work space together.

We tested each material in the renders under morning and evening light before settling on the final shades.

notes.title: Light and texture in built spaces
notes.summary: How light, shadow and material come together to shape a living hall.
notes.body:
A living hall changes through the day. Sheer curtains, timber pillars and a pale floor let the light move slowly across the room instead of arriving all at once.

Texture matters most where the light lands: plaster, wood grain and woven fabric all read differently in low sun.

notes.title: Edges, courtyards and thresholds
notes.summary: Sketches and thoughts from the courtyard of an ongoing residential project.
notes.body:
A courtyard is mostly edges: the step down from a verandah, the line of a wall, the shadow of a roof overhang. Getting those right decides whether the space feels like part of the house.

In this house the planted courtyard sits between the rooms, so every threshold opens onto green.

notes.title: Drawing a room for day and night
notes.summary: Why we show every bedroom in both lights before anything is built.
notes.body:
A bedroom is lived in at both ends of the day, so we draw it twice: once in daylight, once with only its own lamps.

Seeing both views early helps clients choose finishes and lighting with confidence.

notes.title: A terrace under a tiled roof
notes.summary: A covered terrace can become the coolest room in the house.
notes.body:
A sloping tiled roof over an open terrace gives shade, rain cover and a breeze at the same time.

Stone flooring and plants along the edge keep the space cool through the afternoon.
